essential8

Overview

essential8 provides a reproducible R implementation of the American Heart Association Life’s Essential 8 cardiovascular health scoring framework.

It scores both adults aged 20 years or older and children aged 4 months to 19 years, choosing the adult or pediatric AHA definitions row by row from age. See vignette("pediatric-scoring") for pediatric-specific rules.

Installation

CRAN 

install.packages("essential8")

Development 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("thatoneguy006/essential8")

Background

The American Heart Association Life’s Essential 8 (LE8) framework combines eight lifestyle and health components into a composite cardiovascular health score from 0 to 100. essential8 applies the published adult and pediatric scoring bands in one tested workflow and returns all eight component scores plus the composite.

The scoring components are as follows:

  • diet (MEPA, DASH, HEI-2015, or externally supplied percentiles)
  • physical activity (moderate and vigorous activity)
  • smoking
  • sleep
  • BMI
  • blood lipids
  • blood glucose and diabetes status
  • blood pressure (requires both systolic and diastolic measures)

Diet can be scored with one of three measures:

  • MEPA [1]
  • DASH [2]
  • HEI-2015 [3]

MEPA is based on a 16-item questionnaire. DASH and HEI-2015 are based on population indices. More information about the nuances with diet scoring can be found in Diet scoring in Life’s Essential 8, also available through vignette("population-diets", package = "essential8").

Basic use

If this is your first time working with Life Essential 8 scores, you should read the AHA advisory [4] and ?score_le8 before using the package, particularly the input units, population-percentile diet requirements, and optional clinical-judgment adjustments.

Pass a data frame containing inputs for the eight AHA metrics. Missing component values are allowed, and component-specific columns may be omitted when a domain is unavailable. By default, the composite score is calculated when at least seven components are available; this can be changed via min_components with valid thresholds from 1 through 8.

The examples use dplyr and the native pipe (|>, available in R 4.1+). The first scores one adult using MEPA:

library(essential8)
library(dplyr)

patient <- tibble(
  id = "patient_1",
  age = 55,
  sex = "female",

  # MEPA items
  # Daily servings
  olive_oil = 2,
  green_leafy_vegetables = 1,
  other_vegetables = 2,
  whole_grains = 2,
  # Weekly servings
  berries = 3,
  other_fruit = 5,
  meat = 2,
  fish = 3,
  chicken = 2,
  cheese = 1,
  butter_cream = 1,
  beans = 3,
  sweets_and_pastries = 1,
  nuts = 4,
  alcohol = 4,
  # Fast-food meals per week
  fast_food = 0,

  # Physical activity
  moderate_activity_minutes = 90,
  vigorous_activity_minutes = 0,

  # Smoking
  smoking_status = "former",
  years_since_quit = 6,
  current_inhaled_nds = FALSE,
  secondhand_smoke_home = FALSE,

  # Sleep
  sleep_hours = 7.5,

  # BMI
  bmi = 27.5,
  bmi_profile = "general",

  # Blood lipids
  non_hdl_cholesterol = 145,
  lipid_lowering_treatment = FALSE,

  # Diabetes & Glucose
  diabetes = FALSE,
  glucose_measure = "fasting_glucose",
  glucose_value = 95,

  # Blood Pressure
  systolic_bp = 128,
  diastolic_bp = 78,
  antihypertensive_treatment = FALSE
)
patient |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "mepa") |>
  select(id, mepa_total, diet_score, le8_composite_score, le8_category)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   id        mepa_total diet_score le8_composite_score le8_category
#>   <chr>          <int>      <dbl>               <dbl> <chr>       
#> 1 patient_1         14         80                  80 high

The diet_method argument accepts "mepa", "dash", "hei2015", or "percentile". The min_components argument defaults to 7. For diet_method = "mepa", the function calculates mepa_total directly from the 16 screener questions. Their column names must be the column labels shown above. Matching of MEPA, DASH, and HEI-2015 diet columns is case-insensitive; all other input column names are case-sensitive.

The default MEPA sex field is sex; if it is absent, a female column is recognized automatically. Map any other field with, for example, mepa_columns = c(sex = "reported_sex", alcohol = "alc"). For sex, values are trimmed and matched case-insensitively as m/f or male/female. Numeric or character 0/1 values are also accepted, where 0 is male and 1 is female.

For data that use different diet methods, split the rows into separate data frames and call score_le8() separately. Percentile calls use diet_value, containing a DASH or HEI-2015 percentile from 0 to 100. The result appends all eight component scores, n_components, le8_complete, the composite score, and its cardiovascular health category. See ?score_le8 for more information.

DASH and HEI-2015

For population research, use diet_method = "dash" or "hei2015" with raw food and nutrient inputs, an existing diet score, or a percentile. For example, add an existing HEI-2015 score to the adult record above:

patient |>
  mutate(hei2015 = 70) |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "hei2015", reference = "nhanes_2015_2018") |>
  select(id, hei2015, diet_score, le8_composite_score)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   id        hei2015 diet_score le8_composite_score
#>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1 patient_1      70         80                  80

The diet score is converted to LE8 points using the selected reference. See Diet scoring in Life’s Essential 8, also available through vignette("population-diets", package = "essential8"), for the background, scoring rules, input units, and examples.

Incomplete component data

score_le8() preserves ordinary row-level missingness. The composite is the mean of the available component scores when the selected threshold is met:

bind_rows(
  patient,
  patient |> 
    mutate(id = "sleep_missing", sleep_hours = NA_real_)
  ) |>
  score_le8(min_components = 7) |>
  select(id, le8_composite_score, n_components, le8_complete)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   id            le8_composite_score n_components le8_complete
#>   <chr>                       <dbl>        <int> <lgl>       
#> 1 patient_1                    80              8 TRUE        
#> 2 sleep_missing                77.1            7 FALSE

n_components reports how many component scores contributed, while le8_complete is TRUE only when all eight were available. If a component cannot be calculated for any observation, the function emits one consolidated warning identifying every structurally unavailable component.

Imputing missing inputs

By default, score_le8(impute = FALSE) never fills in missing values: the composite averages whichever components are available, which treats a missing component as equal to the average of that person’s other components. With impute = TRUE, score_le8() instead uses multiple imputation [5] with mice [6]:

  1. Check. Observed values are validated first, so data that cannot be scored stop before any imputation.
  2. Impute the inputs, not the scores. Each missing input, such as non-HDL cholesterol or sleep hours, is imputed from age, the participant’s other inputs, and any auxiliary variables you supply. Numeric inputs use predictive mean matching, which only ever imputes values observed in other participants; categorical inputs use logistic or multinomial regression.
  3. Follow the scoring rules. An input is imputed only for participants whose age uses it (adult BMI is never imputed for a child, for example), and combinations the AHA rules do not score, such as diagnosed diabetes without an HbA1c, are never imputed.
  4. Score and pool. Each completed data set is scored and the results are stacked with an .imp column. summary(), summarise(), and plot() pool them with Rubin’s rules, so confidence intervals include the uncertainty from the missing values.
adults <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "le8-adult-example.csv", package = "essential8")
  ) |>
  select(!starts_with("expected_")) |>
  mutate(non_hdl_cholesterol = replace(non_hdl_cholesterol, c(2, 5, 8), NA))

imputed <- adults |>
  score_le8(impute = le8_imputation_control(m = 20, seed = 2026))

summarise(imputed) |>
  filter(measure %in% c("composite", "blood_lipids")) |>
  select(measure, mean, conf.low, conf.high, fmi) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
#>        measure  mean conf.low conf.high  fmi
#> 1    composite 49.06    28.48     69.64 0.19
#> 2 blood_lipids 52.00    24.49     79.51 0.30

The fraction of missing information (fmi) shows how much of each interval’s width comes from the imputed values. le8_imputation_control() sets the number of imputations, a seed, and auxiliary predictors such as an analysis outcome; le8_imputation_setup() shows exactly what will be imputed and how. vignette("case-study") compares complete cases, averaged components, and multiple imputation on simulated data.

Summarize and plot scores

The scored data keep their original class and gain methods for summary(), tidy() (long format), plot() (with ggplot2), and, with dplyr, summarise() without expressions for grouped summaries:

scored <- bind_rows(
  patient,
  patient |> mutate(id = "patient_2", sleep_hours = 5, bmi = 31)
) |>
  score_le8()
summary(scored)
#> LE8 scores: 2 rows (2 adult)
#> Diet method: mepa; min_components: 7
#> Composite score available for 2 of 2; all 8 components for 2.
#> 
#>                   n  mean   sd median         IQR       range
#> LE8 composite     2  73.8  8.8   73.8   70.6-76.9   67.5-80.0
#> Diet              2  80.0  0.0   80.0   80.0-80.0   80.0-80.0
#> Physical activity 2  80.0  0.0   80.0   80.0-80.0   80.0-80.0
#> Nicotine exposure 2  75.0  0.0   75.0   75.0-75.0   75.0-75.0
#> Sleep             2  70.0 42.4   70.0   55.0-85.0  40.0-100.0
#> BMI               2  50.0 28.3   50.0   40.0-60.0   30.0-70.0
#> Blood lipids      2  60.0  0.0   60.0   60.0-60.0   60.0-60.0
#> Blood glucose     2 100.0  0.0  100.0 100.0-100.0 100.0-100.0
#> Blood pressure    2  75.0  0.0   75.0   75.0-75.0   75.0-75.0
#> 
#> Category (rows with a composite score):
#>            n percent
#>   low      0    0.0%
#>   moderate 1   50.0%
#>   high     1   50.0%
summarise(scored)
#> # A tibble: 9 × 10
#>   measure               n n_missing  mean    sd   min   q25 median   q75   max
#>   <fct>             <int>     <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 composite             2         0  73.8  8.84  67.5  70.6   73.8  76.9    80
#> 2 diet                  2         0  80    0     80    80     80    80      80
#> 3 physical_activity     2         0  80    0     80    80     80    80      80
#> 4 nicotine              2         0  75    0     75    75     75    75      75
#> 5 sleep                 2         0  70   42.4   40    55     70    85     100
#> 6 bmi                   2         0  50   28.3   30    40     50    60      70
#> 7 blood_lipids          2         0  60    0     60    60     60    60      60
#> 8 blood_glucose         2         0 100    0    100   100    100   100     100
#> 9 blood_pressure        2         0  75    0     75    75     75    75      75
